thread.title: Apple Stock Dips On Continuing Concerns Over iPhone X Sales

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Dips On Continuing Concerns Over iPhone X Sales
text:
Investment bank Morgan Stanley on Thursday cut its price target on Apple ( AAPL ) stock, bringing up yet more concerns about slowing iPhone X sales.
Morgan Stanley analyst Katy Huberty reduced her price target on Apple to 200 from 205, but maintained her overweight rating on the stock. She cited slowing iPhone X demand as a factor in her price cut.
X Apple's faster-than-expected production ramp of the iPhone X, following earlier snags, could lead to the company beating consensus numbers for the December quarter when it posts its fiscal first quarter results on Feb. 1, Huberty said.
"We agree with the market view of a December-quarter earnings beat," Huberty said in a note to clients. "Apple produced as much as 6 million to 7 million more iPhone X units than we originally modeled."
Apple shares dropped 1.8% to close at 171.11 on the stock market today . Apple hit a record high of 180.10 on Jan. 18 before Wall Street analysts started weighing in with worries about declining demand for the company's flagship smartphone.
IBD'S TAKE: Apple stock has an IBD Composite Rating of 86 out of a best-possible 99. For more analysis on Apple, visit the IBD Stock Checkup . 
In the last two weeks, Apple has been the subject of at least two analyst downgrades and one price-target cut.
For her part, Huberty now expects December-quarter iPhone shipments of 80 million units, vs. her prior view of 76 million. She sees the iPhone average selling price hitting $819 in the quarter, thanks to more premium-priced iPhone X units.
Huberty now believes Apple will earn $4.12 a share on sales of $92.2 billion, up from her earlier forecast of $3.79 and $86.3 billion. On average, analysts are modeling Apple to earn $3.80 a share on sales of $86.75 billion.
Huberty said she disagrees with the prevailing Wall Street view that Apple will guide estimates lower for the March quarter. But she lowered her iPhone sales estimates in the March quarter to reflect a pull-in of iPhone X shipments to the December quarter.
Apple Suppliers Impacted By iPhone Production Cuts Nomura Instinet on Thursday lowered its price targets on seven Asian companies involved in iPhone production, citing recent iPhone order cuts. It downgraded three of those suppliers to neutral from buy.
Of the seven, only Himax Technologies ( HIMX ), is traded in the U.S. Nomura cut its price target on Himax to 10 from 12, but maintained its buy rating.
Himax gained 3.5% to close at 8.36.
"We have observed further order cuts for the iPhone X in the past two weeks," Nomura said in a report. For the first quarter, it now sees production of 18 million units, vs. its prior estimate of 23 million. For the second quarter, it sees 13 million units, down from its earlier estimate of 19 million.
